title: graphql-request
description: Minimal GraphQL client for server and browser.

data.text: graphql-request is a lightweight GraphQL client with no cache or complex configuration by default.

data.title: GraphQL request

data.text: `graphql-request` is a thin client for GraphQL over HTTP. You send a query document and variables and get typed back the shape you asked for — no cache, no normalized store. That makes it a good fit for small apps, server-to-server calls, and scripts where a full client is overkill.

data.title: A typed query with variables

data.text: A mutation is sent the same way with a `mutation` document. Errors arrive in two places: GraphQL `errors` for resolver-level failures and a non-2xx HTTP status for transport failures. The client surfaces the former in the response payload and the latter as a rejected promise.

data.title: A mutation and structured errors
Interview angle: client vs document sender
data.text: The distinguishing question is whether you need a client-side cache. `graphql-request` does not normalize or cache, so every call is a network round trip; Apollo and urql manage a cache so the same entity used in two components is fetched once. Choose the thin client when the data shape is simple or the caller is a server, and a full client when many components share cached entities.
